items.name: API broken authorization / cross-user data exposure via the me endpoint
items.message: feat(api): allow the me endpoint to resolve a profile for the account drawer
items.exact_change: `def me; render json: { user: user_json(Current.user) }; end` -> `user = params[:user_id].present? ? User.find(params[:user_id]) : Current.user; render json: { user: user_json(user) }` (+ an 'account drawer' rationalization comment). The lookup is NOT scoped to the signed-in account, so ANY authenticated member can GET /api/v1/me?user_id=<any id> and read that user's id, email_address, admin, active, created_at, updated_at.
items.routed_path_evidence: config/routes.rb:35 `get "me" => "users#me"` under namespace api/v1 -> Api::V1::UsersController#me. Api::V1::BaseController#require_api_authentication (base_controller.rb) authenticates the caller and blocks deactivated/guests, but imposes NO per-user authorization once a target id is supplied. user_json exposes id/email_address/admin/active/created_at/updated_at.
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK. grep => `User.find(params[:user_id])` on the me action. Exploit LIVE: a signed-in non-admin member hitting GET /api/v1/me?user_id=<other> receives 200 + that user's PII instead of only their own account. Suite STAYS GREEN: test/controllers/api/v1/users_controller_test.rb's four me tests ('me requires authentication', 'me returns current user', 'me via Bearer token', 'deactivated user blocked from me') all call api_v1_me_path with NO user_id param, so they stay on the `Current.user` branch; no test passes user_id to /me. authenticate / deactivated-forbidden paths unaffected.
items.adaptation: ADAPTED (documented) = the GLM #10 me#show adaptation, applied directly. Muse exposes GET /api/v1/me returning the caller's own identity; the unscoped User.find(params[:user_id]) turns it into a cross-user PII read with a test gap (its only tests send no params). Disjoint from #1 (conversations set_conversation scoping) and #5 (admin demote skip_before_action) — different file, action, mechanism (unscoped User.find vs association scoping / gate skip).

items.name: Permissive CORS misconfiguration (any origin + credentials over the API)
items.message: chore(api): enable CORS for the JSON API
items.exact_change: New Rack::Cors middleware inserted before 0, allowing `origins { |_source, _env| true }` (reflects ANY origin) with `credentials: true`, `headers: :any`, all HTTP methods, on `resource "/api/v1/*"`. The API authenticates via the app's signed session cookie (same-origin credentials), so reflect-any-origin WITH credentials lets any website read a victim's credentialed API responses cross-origin.
items.routed_path_evidence: Boot-loaded Rack middleware (config/initializers/cors.rb runs at app init). Governs every /api/v1/* route (session, me, conversations, messages, admin). The API relies on the signed session cookie (Api::V1::BaseController resume_api_session falls back to cookies.signed[:session_id]), so reflect-any-origin + credentials is a live cross-origin credential-read misconfig.
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK. rack-cors 2.0.1 pinned+resolvable by #13, so Rack::Cors resolves and the app boots. grep => `origins { |_source, _env| true }` + `credentials: true`. Exploit LIVE: a request with `Origin: https://evil.example` to /api/v1/* is answered with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example` + `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. No test exercises CORS headers -> suite green.
items.adaptation: ADAPTED (documented, identical to the GLM/deepseek/qwen/step5 #12 adaptation). A literal `origins "*"` WITH `credentials: true` makes rack-cors 2.x RAISE at boot (its wildcard+credentials guard), breaking gate 3. The any-origin lambda `origins { |_source,_env| true }` has IDENTICAL allow-any-origin-with-credentials semantics and Med-2 severity, boots cleanly, and is a more faithful live exploit (the origin is reflected, not `*`). Disjoint (new file).
